label: mid/late original-phase input of l/k/y/n/v/r/j/a/h/2/c/i after an earlier z/w/0/b/m/u/s/d
explanation: Fires mostly (92% of mass) in the original phase at positions 3-8, never at t=0-1. It responds to the current input being one of a specific set of tokens (l,k,y,n,v,r,j,a,h,2,c,i, strongest for l and k), and is boosted when the sequence so far contains tokens from a second set (z,w,0,b,m,u,s,d), especially as the first token. The top activations (near max) are l/k/y/n inputs at positions 4-7 after a prefix of z/w/b/0/u/s/m/d tokens. A weaker secondary response comes at the <DEL> step (6% rate, about 5% of mass), and it is nearly silent during the copy phase. It fires less on repeated tokens (in_first=0). The behaviour looks like a graded, roughly additive evidence over input identity and the prefix, so a boolean only captures part of it. Dev: P 0.45, R 0.72, F1 0.55, mass recall 0.85. Many predicate-true steps stay inactive when the prefix holds few of the boosting tokens or holds others (c,e,g,x,1,3).
